text:
Assistant A is better. It defines the base rate fallacy and gives five distinct examples, as the user asked. Some of them (cherry-picking statistics, anecdotal evidence) are not strictly base rate neglect, but they relate to it loosely and are reasonable given the framing.

Assistant B gives a one-sentence definition and a single example, and that example is confusing. It says a politician claims crime is high when it is actually lower than the national average, which is not clearly a base rate fallacy. It also fails to provide five examples.
